facts: The paper 'Varying the Content of Political Science Surveys to Improve the Survey Experience and Data Quality of Politically Disengaged Respondents' was written by Saskia Bartholomäus and Tobias Gummer.
The article was published on August 11, 2026, in the Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology (DOI: 10.1093/jssam/smaf061).
Political science surveys frequently suffer from biased estimates regarding political attitudes and behavior due to respondents' answering and participation behavior.
The study investigates whether incorporating non-political survey content into political questionnaires improves the survey experience and data quality for politically disengaged respondents.
The authors evaluated data quality specifically in terms of measurement errors and nonresponse errors.
The experimental methodology consisted of two survey experiments conducted across a probability-based panel and a nonprobability-based panel.

The experiments demonstrated that providing a varied questionnaire instead of a purely political questionnaire lowered or even diminished the gap in measurement and nonresponse errors between politically engaged and disengaged participants.
